claims.statement: Manual-dispatch issue example provides GITHUB_TOKEN via GH_TOKEN environment, uses ubuntu-latest and contents read/issues write, then creates an issue in github.repository. GH_TOKEN is shown as env despite prose calling it input; example is not executed or broadly adopted.

Gradle workflow checks out source, configures JDK and setup-gradle caching/execution summaries. Cache and summary functionality are source capabilities, not test results or trusted linked-action review.
Hosted-runner admonition wraps a shared security fragment in WARNING. Correct parent rendering and included warning body require separate resolution.
For fixed-IP hosted runners, private repositories are recommended; fork PR workflows may execute dangerous code on them. Private visibility alone does not prove safe workflow execution.
Conditionals permit supported contexts/expressions only; availability is key-specific and separately linked, not unrestricted context usage.

inputs preserves Boolean types unlike github.event.inputs strings; choice is one selected string. Top-level input limit is 25 on FPT/GHEC and 10 otherwise; payload maximum is 65,535 characters, not bytes.

Importer installation uses gh extension install followed by help inspection; listed commands update/version/configure/audit/forecast/dry-run/migrate have distinct capabilities. Help availability is not migration verification; no extension installed or credentials configured.

Conditional internal-actions sharing stores actions in an internal repository with configured same-organization or enterprise-organization workflow access, without public publication. Internal visibility alone does not enable sharing or grant redistribution rights.
Enterprise Actions introduction calls for a plan before setup; linked planning guidance is not implicitly reviewed or actual rollout approval.
Invalid files in .github/workflows generate failed runs for each new commit according to the source; only valid workflow files should be committed. File existence alone does not show valid behavior.

IP allow-list Actions use requires self-hosted or conditionally static-IP larger hosted runners; Azure private networking uses subnet IPs. Load balancer single-range approach is recommended to reduce list size; runner IP/ranges must be allowed for enterprise communication, not actually configured here.

Java template uses OpenJDK8 x64 PATH; setup-java can select x64/x86 and other versions. Example selects Java11 Temurin x64 through separate action includes. Values are template choices, not universal Java requirements or tested runtime.

JFrog identity mapping example matches issuer https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com and placeholder repository octo-org/octo-repo, conditionally event_name push for Dependabot OIDC support. It is inert trust data, not approved identity mapping or proof of secure claim verification.
JIT runners execute one job; never-used JIT runners are automatically removed. Earlier removal requires removing them on GitHub, and no timeout or actual removal receipt is supplied.
Matrix variables generate multiple job runs from combinations, e.g. language/OS testing. Configuration alone does not prove combinations completed or all requirements tested.

jobs.<job_id>.snapshot uses string or mapping syntax to generate images; each snapshot job creates a separate image and each successful run creates a version. Single-image guidance puts all steps in one job; image generation is not authorized or observed.

Hosted-runner material includes GHES limitation; non-GHES jobs use fresh runs-on image instances, labels/group names and separately included supported labels. Team/GHE Cloud larger runners offer added resources/architectures, not actual entitlement or provisioned capacity.
-latest means GitHub latest stable image, not newest vendor OS. Beta/deprecated images are as-is and excluded from SLA/warranty; beta may lack support. Ubuntu-latest is illustrative.
runs-on selects any runner within a group and may combine labels for finer control; FPT/GHEC group members are larger hosted or self-hosted runners.
Group-only, group-plus-label and conditional GHEC/GHES prefix examples are separate includes. No example bodies or effective group access are certified by this fragment.

runs-on chooses hosted/larger/self-hosted on FPT/GHEC versus self-hosted otherwise; string, variable, array or group/labels mapping supported. Array values are conjunctive: matching all labels, not any label or multiple-machine execution.

String and variable labels can mix; chosen-os dispatch example selects Ubuntu/macOS label on a self-hosted runner. Expressions require quotes unlike simple labels; multiple-machine runs require strategy rather than runs-on array. Example echo is inert.
Self-hosted selection includes a label guidance reusable and shows [self-hosted, linux], with concept/use links. Example does not instantiate a runner, review included guidance or prove label access.
